Monte Carlo intervals for response surface parameters

Source: R/rsa-mplus-inference.R
rsa_mplus_draws.Rd

Draws the polynomial weights b1 to b5 of a fitted Mplus response surface from their asymptotic sampling distribution (a multivariate normal with the estimates as means and the TECH3 covariance matrix) and computes the surface parameters on each draw. This gives intervals for parameters whose delta-method standard errors are poor, such as ratios, without refitting the model, and draws on which any further function of the surface can be evaluated.

Usage

rsa_mplus_draws(
  model,
  outcome = NULL,
  pred_x = NULL,
  pred_y = NULL,
  pred_x2 = NULL,
  pred_xy = NULL,
  pred_y2 = NULL,
  rsa_model = NULL,
  n = 10000L,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

model

Path to an Mplus .out file, an object returned by MplusAutomation::readModels(), an mplusObject containing results, or an rsa_mplus_workflow() object.

outcome

Dependent variable label from the Mplus regression table. Inferred for generated RSA-Mplus workflows.

pred_x

Label of the linear X predictor in the Mplus output. Inferred for generated RSA-Mplus workflows.

pred_y

Label of the linear Y predictor in the Mplus output. Inferred for generated RSA-Mplus workflows.

pred_x2

Label of the squared X term in the Mplus output. Inferred for generated RSA-Mplus workflows.

pred_xy

Label of the XY interaction term in the Mplus output. Inferred for generated RSA-Mplus workflows.

pred_y2

Label of the squared Y term in the Mplus output. Inferred for generated RSA-Mplus workflows.

rsa_model

Name of the fitted model in the RSA package's model family. Terms that this model sets to zero may be missing from the Mplus output, and their labels are optional. One of "full", "additive", "IA", "SQD", "SRRR", "SRR", "RR", "SSQD", "SRSQD", "null", "onlyx2", "onlyy2", "onlyx", "onlyy", "mean", "diff", "weak", or "strong". If NULL (the default), the model that create_rsa_mplus_model() generated for a workflow, and otherwise "full". Also passed to RSA::plotRSA() as model. See Details.

n

Number of draws.

probs

Lower and upper quantile of the reported intervals.

seed

Optional seed, set locally for the draws.

Value

An object of class rsa_mplus_draws, a list with

  • draws: a data frame with one row per draw.

  • summary: a data frame with the parameter, its estimate est computed from the point estimates, the standard deviation se of the draws, and the lower and upper quantiles.

  • rsa_model, n, and probs.

Details

The model must have been estimated by maximum likelihood with TECH1 and TECH3 in the OUTPUT command, for example blocks = list(OUTPUT = "STDYX CINTERVAL TECH1 TECH3;") in create_rsa_mplus_model(). Bayesian models have no TECH3; use their posterior draws (BPARAMETERS) instead.

Terms that share a parameter in the model, for example through a shared label, share its draws. The restrictions of rsa_model are imposed on the draws and on the estimates: terms the model sets to zero are 0, and terms it defines from others (such as b4 = -2*b5 in "SRR") are computed from them. This also removes the rounding of the printed estimates, which do not satisfy the restrictions exactly.

Besides b1 to b5, the draws hold the surface parameters a1 to a5 (cs, cc, is, ic, and a5 in the generated MODEL CONSTRAINT), and the parameters specific to rsa_model in create_rsa_mplus_model(): the ridge parameters c, s, bm, and a4r, or the stationary point and principal axes. Ratios can be undefined or extreme in single draws, so their intervals are quantiles and the standard deviation in se may be large.

Mplus prints estimates and covariances with limited precision. The draws are therefore centred on estimates rounded to three decimals.

See also

RSA_mplus(), rsa_mplus_supported_range()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fitted <- rsa_mplus_workflow(
  data = dat,
  measurement = measurement,
  rsa_model = "SRR",
  blocks = list(OUTPUT = "TECH1 TECH3;"),
  modelout = "rsa_srr.inp",
  run = TRUE
)
intervals <- rsa_mplus_draws(fitted, seed = 1)
intervals$summary
} # }
